Subject: QBR slate stability checkpoint, launch cadence and cross-team escalations

Team —

As we close the quarter I want a tight snapshot of where product + eng are on the QBR slate stability items and a short escalation path for anything that could impact our June launch commitments to AstraTech. Please treat this as the single source item for leadership review and for the customer-facing note.

What I need by EOD Tuesday (2027-06-22):
- Updated stability matrix (tabbed: infra, model, infra-config, rollout) with owner and mitigation ETA. See attached draft.
- Launch cadence timeline with canary windows, rollback gates, and SLO deltas.
- Top 3 delivery risks with proposed mitigations and a comms line to share with AstraTech if we hit any of them.

I've attached a starting matrix and a draft timeline (small changes expected). Marcus, please lead infra and rollout rows; Karthik, lead model/regression rows; Monica, owner-side/customer comms. Vivek, flag anything you want explicitly escalated to execs. Marissa — coordinate QA signoff cutoff and contingency for delayed canaries.

Attachments: [Attachment: qbr_stability_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)], [Attachment: launch_cadence_timeline.png (image)]

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR slate stability checkpoint, launch cadence and cross-team escalations

Hannah — quick update against the matrix attached. High-level:

1) Infra pool expansion (infra) — risk: delayed GPU provisioning in us-west-2 (impact: throughput for canary). Mitigation: bring two reserved machines online from Dedicated pool; ETA: 2027-06-23 (owner: marcus.lin).

2) KV cache regression (model infra) — risk: recent release of caching optimization caused 0.8% latency tail increase on long sequences. Mitigation: revert last optimization for canary traffic; ETA: immediate for canary, full rollback in 24 hours (owner: karthik.iyer).

3) Canary gating and observability (release) — risk: thresholds not aligned with AstraTech SLAs. Mitigation: add additional trace hooks and a stricter threshold in the first 10m of canary traffic; ETA: 2027-06-22 08:00 (owner: marissa.cole).

I've updated the attached spreadsheet with owners and ETAs for the first pass. Two asks: 1) Karthik — confirm revert plan and perf impact numbers; 2) Monica — confirm customer comms we can send if we need to shift canary window by 24–48h.

Thanks,
Marcus
Sr. Engineering Manager

Short update on the KV cache regression:
- Root cause: micro-optimization in the attention cache evictor that increased path length for certain sequence shapes.
- Impact: ~0.8% p99 tail increase for sequences > 1k tokens in our internal perf suite.
- Plan: feature-flag revert for canary traffic + extended tracing for the first 30 min. Revert can be staged in 30m and validated in 2 hours.
- Risk: there is a small accuracy delta with older quantized kernels; will validate against eval set during the rollback window.

I'll post a short runbook in the drive folder and flag if we need a hold. ETA: revert staged at 2027-06-22T02:30Z, validation complete by 2027-06-22T04:30Z (owner: karthik.iyer).

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
